title: Slot-bound assignments
contract: MIDI and computer-key assignments to Session slots belong to the slot, not the contained clip. Clip launch effects remain with the Session/clip-launch owners; replacement, move and delete identity rules beyond this distinction remain U.

title: Assigned MIDI notes and track input
contract: The chapter describes a MIDI note assigned to remote control as unavailable for MIDI-track instrument input. This is a documentary exclusivity role, not a general channel/port interception, note-off or MPE dispatch law.

title: Named surface setup
contract: For a natively supported surface, choose its name in Control Surface settings and choose input/output ports in adjacent columns. The source describes up to six supported surfaces simultaneously; an absent chooser entry leads to manual setup, not proof of incompatibility or any particular profile protocol.

title: Conditional preset-dump setup
contract: Some surfaces require a preset dump and expose an enabled Dump button for setup. The hardware must first be ready to receive it using its own documented preparation. No universal dump requirement, payload, success detector, timeout or device-state restoration follows.

title: Manual override of instant assignments
contract: Manual assignments may override instant mappings, with Remote enabled for the relevant ports. The override scope, conflict arbitration, release/restoration and host effect are not established by this chapter or by the finite configuration release.

title: Selection-following instant control
contract: Instant mappings are described as following selected devices. Exact per-surface parameter banks, unsupported devices, selection/focus races and host delivery remain U; this does not complete the existing host/bank unknowns.

title: Lock menu and status affordances
contract: For a surface that supports device locking, the device-title context menu Lock to entry enables/disables its lock; the available surface names correspond to configured surfaces, and a hand icon indicates locked status. Some surfaces do not support locking. This clause owns the generic entry/status affordance only.

title: Lock focus and arming context
contract: The manual describes supported device locking as retaining access across focus changes and describes a default automatic instrument lock when a MIDI track is armed. These are documentary contexts only: capability, arm-selection interaction, constructor default, bank contents and host lock effects remain U under the existing mapping owner.

title: Manual setup entry boundary
contract: An unlisted control surface can be set up for manual mapping through MIDI Ports. This workflow uses the routing owner's Remote input/output roles, rather than redefining Track/Sync/Remote or promising arbitrary hardware support.

title: Feedback prerequisite
contract: Physical/visual feedback surfaces require the output-port Remote role so value changes can be reflected by faders or LEDs. The general port switch belongs to routing; feedback eligibility, startup state, bytes, loops and physical movement law remain U.

title: Incoming activity indicator
contract: The Control Bar MIDI indicators flash when Live recognizes incoming MIDI. This is an activity indicator role, not proof of a mapping, source identity, output feedback, MIDI-track admission or hardware synchronization.

title: Takeover selection context
contract: The source presents None, Pick-Up and Value Scaling for absolute controls used across destination banks. This clause supplies documentary chooser vocabulary and setup context only; finite transforms, previous-value history, exemptions and precision stay with REQ-MIDI-USER-005/010 and midi-config-v4. Target displayed labels/default remain unproven.

title: Mapping Browser view and columns
contract: The Mapping Browser is shown for the active manual MIDI, key or Macro mapping mode and lists that mode's mappings with control element, parameter path/name and Min/Max. This owns common browser presentation; rack Macro assignment/delegation remains with device-racks.

title: Range edit and inversion entrypoints
contract: Mapping Browser Min/Max entries can be edited, and a context command inverts them. This is an editing affordance only: accepted domains, parsing, stored representation, target scaling/rounding and resulting values remain with existing finite owners or U.

title: Delete a selected mapping
contract: The Mapping Browser deletes selected mappings with Backspace on Windows or Delete on Mac. Restoration of target value, control ownership, held-input cleanup and Undo grouping are not specified.

title: Instant mappings outside the browser
contract: Context-based instant mappings are not listed in the Mapping Browser. Absence from this manual-mapping list does not prove absence of active instant control.

title: MIDI Map Mode entry and exit
contract: The MIDI switch enters Map Mode, highlighting assignable controls blue and exposing Mapping Browser; the switch exits and hides the browser. Reentering allows review. Ctrl+Alt+B on Windows or Cmd+Option+B on Mac opens a closed Browser in this context; exact geometry/color metrics are not specified.

title: Create a manual MIDI assignment
contract: In MIDI Map Mode, select an eligible parameter and send a controller MIDI message; the new assignment is listed in Mapping Browser. Supported message grammar, duplicate/conflict resolution, transaction boundaries and host delivery are not established here.

title: Note-target roles
contract: The source assigns note gestures to switches/options and describes a single note toggling a variable parameter between endpoints, while a note range supplies discrete spaced values. Session slot input follows its Launch Mode owner. Exact note grammar, toggle dispatch, spacing/interpolation, endpoint codec and timing remain U.

title: Chromatic slot-range assignment gesture
contract: For a chromatic Session-slot note range, the documented assignment gesture holds a root key, then a lower and higher key to define bounds. The root is described as default transposition. Transposition, note allocation, range codec and sound remain U.

title: Absolute input family boundary
contract: The chapter describes absolute control input, pitch bend and high-resolution absolute input with target-dependent effects. Its numerical threshold/range examples are retained as source context only. The released configuration transforms remain scoped to their stated parameters/assumptions; no manual-Learn, switch, radio or slot law is imported from them.

title: Relative-mode detection and selection
contract: The source names Signed Bit, Signed Bit 2, Bin Offset and Twos Complement families plus linear variants. For unsupported-native surfaces it describes detection of type/acceleration, aided by a slow left movement during assignment; a Status Bar mode chooser offers a suggestion and manual selection. Detection success, exact UI list and mapping to configuration tokens remain U.

title: Relative target roles
contract: Relative increment/decrement gestures are described as slot down/up equivalents, switch on/off and option forward/back; continuous interpretation depends on controller type. Exact codecs, steps, acceleration, endpoint/wrap and event dispatch remain U here; existing released relative computations are not broadened.

title: Relative Session mapping strip
contract: Both MIDI and Key Map modes expose a strip of assignable controls below the Session grid for relative navigation/launch roles. This is a mapping entrypoint, not a launch/scene scheduling law.

title: Highlighted-scene navigation assignment
contract: The strip offers up/down highlighted-scene controls assignable to keys/notes/controllers and a scene-number box assignable to a MIDI controller for scrolling. Endpoint/wrap, number encoding, relative decoder and focus precedence remain U.

title: Highlighted-scene launch and cancel entrypoints
contract: The strip offers launch-highlighted-scene and cancel-triggered-scene assignment targets. Scene launch/cancel behavior and Select Next Scene on Launch stay with REQ-SESSION-VIEW-010/011; this clause adds only mapped entrypoints.

title: Per-track highlighted-row clip launch target
contract: The strip supplies per-track assignable controls to launch the clip at the highlighted scene. This is a target-entrypoint role only; empty-slot recording/stop, clip launch timing and playing/selection changes remain with existing owners or U.

title: Highlighted-scene viewport role
contract: Relative Session mapping is described as keeping the highlighted scene centered in Session View. No pixel metric, edge-of-list padding, hidden-row or resizing policy is established.

title: Clip View mapping follows selection context
contract: Mappings created for Clip View controls can affect different selected clips, including multi-selection; the manual recommends relative controls to avoid value jumps. Shared panel/selection UI stays with Clip View. This is not a numerical smoothing guarantee, target identity formula or general multi-edit transaction law.

title: Key Map Mode entry and exit
contract: The KEY switch enters Key Map Mode with red-highlighted assignable controls and Mapping Browser; the View menu can show a hidden Browser. Exiting hides Mapping Browser, and reentering allows review. This does not define global shortcut or Computer MIDI Keyboard dispatch.

title: Create a computer-key assignment
contract: In Key Map Mode select a red-highlighted eligible control and press a computer key; Mapping Browser displays the new assignment. Only highlighted controls are offered for mapping; duplicate keys, reserved chords, layouts and text-focus interception remain U.

title: Computer-key target roles
contract: Mapped computer keys are described as operating slot clips according to Launch Mode, toggling switches and cycling option buttons. This is manual key mapping, distinct from Computer MIDI Keyboard note generation; global shortcuts, key-repeat, held releases and precedence remain U.

title: Key and focus arbitration
contract: Layout/IME, Computer MIDI Keyboard, global shortcuts, text/modal/plugin focus, navigation preferences, repeats and duplicate input-source precedence remain unknown.

title: Manual mapping numerical and protocol outcomes
contract: Manual MIDI Learn admission, message bytes, relative detection/codecs, scales, display curves, thresholds, takeover application, feedback and sample/event timing remain unknown beyond separately released finite clauses.

title: Per-profile and host behavior
contract: Generic setup does not specify the 149 inventoried controller directories, Push generations, arbitrary scripts, user-profile discovery/reload, exact device bank contents, host lock/arm effects or preset-dump protocols.

title: Assignment domains and malformed controls
contract: Invalid/unsupported controls/messages/ranges, empty or deleted targets, range gestures, exhausted surface rows, and cancellation commit points lack output oracles.

title: Persistence, undo, automation and teardown
contract: Set/global ownership, save/reopen/migration, undo grouping, automation override, source loss/reconnection, reset history and cleanup during held input/device deletion remain required unknowns.
